item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission examined procurement misconduct risks through investigations, audits of five local governments and a review of financial governance at the City of Stirling.
item.support: describe audits carried out on behalf of the Commission into the capacity of five local governments to prevent, identify and deal with misconduct in procurement

item.text: It found that procurement and financial governance weaknesses, including insufficient risk assessment, left local governments exposed to fraud and corruption.
item.support: This is exacerbated by a lack of risk assessment by many local governments in their procurement processes

item.text: The Commission favoured prevention across the sector and considered external procurement audit necessary.
item.support: In the Commission's view a whole-of-sector approach, with a focus on prevention, is needed.

item.text: Its two recommendations sought Auditor General oversight of local governments and active departmental scrutiny of their procurement risk reviews.
item.support: The Commission recommends that the jurisdiction of the Auditor General be extended to include local governments.

item.quote: In the Commission's view a whole-of-sector approach, with a focus on prevention, is needed.
There is a need for external audit of local government procurement.
